column5: Look: 2.5D, pixel sprites on a flat plane moving through a lit 3D sea: parallax depth layers, volumetric god-rays near the surface, black-blue deep water, bioluminescent teal and amber accents (teal = danger and creatures, amber = the tavern, safety and loot). Bosses are monumental dark-fantasy silhouettes (a drowned knight, a great eel, a coral-crowned leviathan) drawn large against the dark. The tavern is warm amber firelight in a stone cellar. Every figure drawn: no emoji, no plain circles.
References: Dave the Diver (pixel sprites in a 3D sea, the dive and the catch), Elden Ring (monumental dark-fantasy bosses and mood), Dark Souls (stamina, roll, punish windows, dropped souls).
View: 2.5D · Camera: side-on follow2d with depth parallax.
Side-on stamina combat: light and heavy attack, roll with brief invulnerability, guard, flask that can be interrupted
3 depths, each a short minion area then a boss; 4 minion kinds each attacking differently
Boss hunt: bosses limp when hurt, lose parts and flee to rest, then return
Catch: kill or reel in fish, sea creatures and treasure, kept in a bag
Tavern (bonfire): rest to heal, refill flasks and save; sell the catch, cook it into a buff, spend souls on levels, upgrade the weapon
Progressive difficulty per depth: new minion kind, tougher stats, boss second phase
Drop-on-death with a retrievable bloodstain
Tavern: sell, cook and upgrade · in the slice
Catch and fishing: kill and reel in · in the slice
Progression: levels and weapon upgrades · in the slice
Boss hunt: limp, part loss, flee · in the slice
You wake at the tavern's hearth and walk to the dive door.

You descend, meet one drifting minion that teaches the stamina bar (swing, roll through its lunge), take your first catch, and the hook pays off: a boss's silhouette glides across the dark below while the tavern's amber light fades behind you.
Real trouble within the first minute or two: an elite minion that punishes rolling away.
Each depth adds a minion kind with a new attack, and bosses gain a second phase; minions are tougher and faster as you descend.
A death drops souls and catch where you fell and returns you to the tavern; dying before you retrieve them loses them for good.
Never trivially easy, never a wall in the first minute.
